# Sāsanapaṭṭhāna (Ne 37)

**ID:** Ne 37  
**Section:** Netti (ne)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Sāsanapaṭṭhāna  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0519m.mul5.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0519m.mul5.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna* ("The Pattern of the Dispensation") constitutes the final subsection of the *Paṭiniddesavāra* ("Further Explanation") in the *Nettippakaraṇa*, following the *Hāravibhaṅga*, *Hārasampāta*, and *Nayasamuṭṭhāna* [Caudron 2000]. Within the hermeneutical framework of the *Netti*, it embodies an extensive classification and mapping of Piṭaka passages according to their leading themes and thoughts [Law 1923]. Because its categories and classifications extend beyond the basic method of sixteen modes (*hārā*) and five guide-lines (*nayā*) established in the *Uddesavāra*, scholars have examined whether this section was integral to the core interpretive methodology or represents a later stratum of commentary [Balasooriya et al. 1980; Caudron 2000].

- Passage-level parallels: Pe 3 Suttādhiṭṭhānatatiyabhūmi; Ne 2 Uddesavāra; Vv 47 Pītavimānavatthu; Tha-Ap 1 Buddhaapadāna
- Resembling parallels: Vv 6 Paṭhamanāvāvimānavatthu; Vv 7 Dutiyanāvāvimānavatthu; Vv 8 Tatiyanāvāvimānavatthu

**Sources**

- [Balasooriya et al. 1980] Balasooriya et al. (eds.), Buddhist Studies in honour of Walpola Rahula (1980) — Discussed the relationship of Sāsanapaṭṭhāna categories to the basic method of the Uddesavāra.
- [Caudron 2000] Marian Winston Caudron, Guide to Skillful Means: Reexamining the Netti-Pakaraṇa's Modes and Methods (2000) — Described the structural placement of Sāsanapaṭṭhāna in the Paṭiniddesavāra and textual stratification.
- [Law 1923] Bimala Charan Law, The Life and Work of Buddhaghosa (1923) — Noted that Sāsanapaṭṭhāna classifies Piṭaka passages according to leading thoughts.
